Step 0: Rules first: Annex A and the Designated Targets

Before any lab access

What to do

  1. Read the Legal Notice, then sign Annex A before any lab access, with the A.2 initials for §7.2 (monitoring and capture) and §7.4 (defensive configuration changes). The e-signature page will be provided separately.
  2. Write down the Designated Targets of this lab: MON-01 (monitoring server, 192.168.56.10), PC-ACCT-01 (accounting workstation, 192.168.56.21) and, optionally, SRV-FILE-01 (file server, 192.168.56.20).
  3. Keep all of them inside your Authorized Lab Environment: your own virtual machines on the isolated host-only network 192.168.56.0/24.

Do not

  • Do not monitor, scan or capture your home Wi-Fi, the College network, an employer's systems or a classmate's computer.
  • Do not use a real organization or real people: Val-des-Pins is fictional, and real systems need a written authorization (Annex D) that is not part of this lab.
  • Do not record classes or share lab machines, passwords, this page or your files.

Why

Authorization is the rule that governs everything else. Monitoring a system without its owner's permission can be an offence under the Criminal Code of Canada (sections 342.1 and 184), and logs about people are personal information under Québec's Law 25. If you are not sure that you are authorized, you are not: stop and ask.

Step 1: Prepare the virtual lab

Isolation and snapshots

What to do

  1. Install VirtualBox 7.2 from its official site and compare its SHA-256 (Secure Hash Algorithm, 256 bits) value with the published checksum list.
  2. File, Tools, Network Manager, Host-only Networks, Create: address 192.168.56.1/24, DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) server off.
  3. Create MON-01: Ubuntu (64-bit), 8 GB (gigabytes) of memory, 4 processors (2 if your computer has only 4), 80 GB disk; Adapter 1 NAT (network address translation), Adapter 2 Host-only.
  4. Create PC-ACCT-01: Windows 11 (64-bit), 4 GB, 2 processors, 64 GB, the same two adapters.
  5. Take a snapshot (a saved state you can return to) of each machine before every step.

Do not

  • Do not use a "Bridged" adapter: it puts the lab machines on your home or College network.
  • Do not copy personal files into the lab machines.
  • Do not start a step without a snapshot.

Why

The host-only network keeps lab traffic away from other people's networks (§6.4). NAT lets the machines download updates, but nothing outside can reach them through it. Monitoring tools can fill a disk or crash a machine: a snapshot is your way back.

Step 2: Ubuntu Server on MON-01, first updates

Criterion 3.3

What to do

  1. Download Ubuntu Server 24.04 LTS (long-term support); on your computer run Get-FileHash .\ubuntu-24.04*.iso -Algorithm SHA256 and compare with SHA256SUMS.
  2. Install with host name mon-01, user tech, and "Install OpenSSH server" ticked (SSH: Secure Shell).
  3. Run sudo timedatectl set-timezone America/Toronto, then sudo apt update && sudo apt full-upgrade -y && sudo reboot.
  4. Give the host-only adapter (usually enp0s8, shown by ip a) the fixed address 192.168.56.10/24 in /etc/netplan/60-lab.yaml, then sudo netplan apply.

Do not

  • Do not install Ubuntu 26.04 for this lab: Wazuh 4.14 does not list it yet.
  • Do not skip the checksum comparison.
  • Do not leave the time zone wrong: time-based alerts would fire at the wrong hours.

Why

Criterion 3.3 asks for a proper installation of updates, and the update log goes into Section 4 of your report. A checksum proves that the file is the one the publisher released (§14, Annex C).

Step 3: Install Wazuh on MON-01

Criteria 3.1 and 3.3

What to do

  1. Check the address on VirusTotal, then run curl -sO https://packages.wazuh.com/4.14/wazuh-install.sh and sudo bash ./wazuh-install.sh -a (all-in-one, 10 to 20 minutes).
  2. Keep the passwords: sudo tar -O -xvf wazuh-install-files.tar wazuh-install-files/wazuh-passwords.txt.
  3. Disable the Wazuh repository (package source) so that no update changes the version during the lab: sudo sed -i "s/^deb /#deb /" /etc/apt/sources.list.d/wazuh.list.
  4. Record the version with sudo /var/ossec/bin/wazuh-control info, then open https://192.168.56.10 from your computer and log in as admin.

Do not

  • Do not publish the dashboard on the Internet or share the admin password.
  • Do not download the assistant from a mirror or a video description.
  • Do not upgrade Wazuh in the middle of the lab.

Why

Wazuh was selected in Class 8: free and open source, it collects events, applies rules, shows alerts and sends e-mail, and for 1 to 25 agents it runs on 4 virtual processors and 8 GB of memory. Like every monitoring tool, it is lawful in your lab and an offence on a system you are not authorized to touch (§6.5).

Step 4: Connect PC-ACCT-01 (Windows agent)

Criterion 3.4

What to do

  1. Install Windows 11 Enterprise from the Microsoft Evaluation Center (local account vdp.admin) and run Windows Update.
  2. In PowerShell as Administrator: New-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias "Ethernet 2" -IPAddress 192.168.56.21 -PrefixLength 24 and net user test.user "Lab-2026-Test!" /add.
  3. Download wazuh-agent-4.14.8-1.msi, run Get-FileHash with -Algorithm SHA512 and compare with the .sha512 value (SHA-512: Secure Hash Algorithm, 512 bits) of the Wazuh packages list.
  4. Install with msiexec.exe /i, WAZUH_MANAGER="192.168.56.10" and WAZUH_AGENT_NAME="PC-ACCT-01" (MSI: Microsoft Installer), then NET START WazuhSvc.
  5. In the dashboard, Agents must show PC-ACCT-01 Active.

Do not

  • Do not install an agent on your own host computer or on anyone else's device.
  • Do not install an agent newer than the manager.
  • Do not use your own account for tests: use test.user.

Why

Need N-01 of your monitoring plan requires the events of PC-ACCT-01. An agent installed on a device without its owner's consent can break the Criminal Code and Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation (section 8), so it goes only on your own lab machines (§7.2).

5

Step 5: Build the two baselines

Criterion 3.4

What to do

  1. B1, measured: keep both machines running 48 hours or more, use PC-ACCT-01 normally by day and at night, then count the alerts per hour with jq into b1_hourly.txt (the command is in the Lab 02 guide).
  2. B2, FW-01 stand-in: copy the Class 12 code/ folder to MON-01 and create vdp_fw01_standin.py from the guide.
  3. Run python3 vdp_fw01_standin.py <your student number>, then python3 class12_baseline_thresholds.py.
  4. Paste the threshold sheet in Section 5 and justify k; create /var/log/vdp/fw01-volume.log.

Do not

  • Do not invent numbers or reuse the Class 12 example values.
  • Do not use real traffic from home or work.
  • Do not use another student's number.

Why

A threshold has to come from measured normal activity (Lesson 3.4), not from a guess. The lab has no real firewall, so the FW-01 (firewall) volume is synthetic, as §6.7 requires; your student number makes your data unique (§18).

Step 6: Write the decoder and the rules

Criteria 3.2 and 3.5

What to do

  1. In /var/ossec/etc/ossec.conf, add the volume file as a source (<localfile>).
  2. Write the decoder in /var/ossec/etc/decoders/local_decoder.xml (XML: Extensible Markup Language).
  3. Write rules AL-01, AL-02 and AL-07 (AL: alert, from Table 3.5.A) in /var/ossec/etc/rules/local_rules.xml (version 1.0); add AL-05 after test T5 and your variation (AL-03, AL-04 or AL-06).
  4. Test with sudo /var/ossec/bin/wazuh-logtest, then apply with sudo systemctl restart wazuh-manager.

Do not

  • Do not edit the files under /var/ossec/ruleset/: updates overwrite them.
  • Do not add any active response or blocking (§7.4).
  • Do not restart the manager before the rule passes wazuh-logtest.

Why

Rules turn the suspicious behaviours of your catalogue (criterion 3.2) into alerts with a level (criterion 3.5). Detection rules are defensive changes: test them in the lab first and keep every version (§7.4).

7

Step 7: Notify: a local lab mailbox

Criterion 3.5

What to do

  1. Run sudo apt install -y postfix mailutils and choose "Local only", mail name mon-01.
  2. In ossec.conf, inside <global>: email_notification yes, smtp_server localhost, email_from wazuh@mon-01, email_to tech@localhost, email_maxperhour 12 (SMTP: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol).
  3. Inside <alerts>: email_alert_level 10. Restart the manager and read the mail with mail.
  4. Write your notification matrix in Section 7: recipient role, channel, delay, acknowledgement, escalation.

Do not

  • Do not use a real e-mail address or a public relay.
  • Do not send text messages from the lab.
  • Do not remove the hourly e-mail limit.

Why

An alert must reach the person responsible (Table 3.5.E), but lab messages stay inside the lab (§6.4, §7.4). Level 10 and above (High, Critical) goes by e-mail; Medium stays on the dashboard.

8

Step 8: Test, tune and record

Criterion 3.5

What to do

  1. Run the tests in this order with test.user: T2, T1, T3, T4, T6, then T5 last.
  2. T1: runas /user:test.user cmd with a wrong password 5 times within 2 minutes; T2: only 3 times; T3: the right password just after T1.
  3. T4: append the VDP-VOLUME lines of the threshold program to /var/log/vdp/fw01-volume.log; T5: wevtutil cl Security as Administrator.
  4. Record each result in Table 3.5.F and compute precision and recall. After a failed test, tune (version 1.1), rerun every test and record the change in Table 3.5.G.

Do not

  • Do not test with your own account or outside the lab.
  • Do not clear the Security log before the other tests.
  • Do not change a result to make it look better.

Why

Only a test proves that a rule fires when it should and stays quiet when it should (criterion 3.5). Reporting honestly is part of the Code of Ethics (§9).
